name: Bailey Moran
life: “I still remember having to tell my history twice in the same waiting room.” On Friday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Bailey stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I have no claim on her evenings and want an introduction to the person who will read what she wrote about me.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. Bailey has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with salt-and-pepper curls. Bailey raises one eyebrow long before saying yes during a conversation.
personality: Bailey loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Bailey remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To get a personal introduction to the successor.
family: Vincent Farah is Bailey’s younger cousin. Bailey calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Vincent leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Five missing lunches*, Vincent says, “My son painted a whale on the lid. It's the only thing he drew before his hand operation.”
connections: Sam Lim. The longtime patient meets the successor while the departing physician can still make the introduction.

reactions.situation: The incoming doctor is compared with the old one
reactions.response: Bailey gives the new doctor a chance to speak before retelling the old doctor's habits.
